# Strategy Comparison Skill

**Purpose:** Compare WiFi connection performance between the two device strategies using passive log analysis.

**When to use:**
- Determining which connection strategy works better
- A/B testing WiFi improvements
- Analyzing long-term connectivity patterns
- Making decisions about dwell vs. auto strategy priority

## Quick Start

```powershell
.venv\Scripts\python.exe skills/strategy-comparison/compare_strategies.py
```

## Output

| Metric | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Attempts | Total connection attempts for that path |
| Success rate | % of attempts that succeeded |
| Avg connect time | Mean time to successful connection |
| Median connect | Middle value (50th percentile) |
| P95 connect | 95th percentile time (worst 5%) |
| Std deviation | Variability of connect times |
| Channel hits | Which WiFi channels used most often |

## Options

| Flag | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `--base-url http://<ip>:8080` | Validate different device |
| `--min-samples 20` | Set minimum samples for reliability (default: 10) |
| `--save-json results/comparison.json` | Export results as JSON |

## WiFi Strategies

| Strategy | Scan Dwell | Fallback | Typical Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dwell** | 200ms | Uses configured AP hint | Fast |
| **auto** | 500ms | Pure auto-discovery | Slower but more reliable |

Device alternates between them on every reconnect attempt.

## Reliability

Verdict flagged as "unreliable" if either path has fewer samples than `--min-samples` threshold.

## Interpretation

**dwell is better if:**
- Success rate ≥ auto
- Connect time < auto
- P95 within acceptable range

**auto is better if:**
- Success rate significantly higher
- Justifies slightly longer connect time
- More stable across conditions
